Software already executes a fence (sfence.vma/hfence.gvma/hfence.vvma/mfence.pa) when it reuses any of the identifiers.

What are the advantages of using fence.time instead of finer-grained fences?

I think we could even define the behavior above as a separate extension, because it doesn't require any changes to the architecture, and all secure implementation should already be doing it.

body:
Discussed in the meeting.
Executing existing TLB fences does not provide a clear intent to change the protection domain, which could result in pointless protection.  Reusing the IDs should be rare enough to make any performance impact of the fence.time moot.
fence.time might need changes to be applicable for this purpose.
